fields.Name: NetForum Enterprise

Configuration.AuthFlowNote: NetForum Enterprise xWeb uses a two-step token auth model. Step 1: POST to <tenantBaseURL>/xWeb/JSON/Authenticate with HTTP Basic auth (Base64-encoded username:password in Authorization header). The response returns a Bearer token in the WWW-Authenticate response header (format: "Bearer token = <guid>") and/or as a JSON body field. Step 2: All subsequent xWeb JSON calls carry the token as "Authorization: Bearer <token>". The SOAP mode alternative uses a SOAP AuthorizationToken header element (<AuthorizationToken><Token>...</Token></AuthorizationToken>). Source: connector source code (NetForumConnector.ts:326-357) + credential type schema (netforum-token.schema.json). WSDL evidence: Authenticate operation in WSDL (SOAPAction http://www.avectra.com/2005/Authenticate). Note: token validity window not documented publicly; connector defaults to 1-hour TTL (ExpiresAt = Date.now() + 3600*1000).
Configuration.AuthHeaderPatternNote: JSON-over-xWeb mode: the Bearer token obtained from /xWeb/JSON/Authenticate is passed on every subsequent call as "Authorization: Bearer <token>". SOAP xWeb mode: token is in the SOAP AuthorizationToken header element, NOT an HTTP header. Source: WSDL (AuthorizationToken defined in XSD), connector code BuildHeaders(), netforum-token.schema.json.
Configuration.TransportModeNote: The canonical xWeb transport is SOAP 1.1/1.2 over HTTPS (netFORUMXML.asmx). A JSON shim (/xWeb/JSON/<MethodName>) wraps the same SOAP methods in a JSON envelope. The MJ connector uses the JSON shim (simpler HTTP + Bearer token). The SOAP mode is the authoritative contract — the WSDL is the machine-readable spec. Source: WSDL (netForumXML_asm.wsdl, 5.9 MB, 277 ops, Tier-1 ExplicitStatement) and connector code.
Configuration.SOAPNamespaceNote: Avectra-era namespace retained by Community Brands. All WSDL operations and DataObjectType schemas use this namespace. Source: WSDL namespace declaration confirmed on both ASM (myasm.asm.org) and APCO (apconetforum.org) public instances.
Configuration.NavigationBaseURLNote: The xWeb endpoint is per-tenant. There is no single canonical host. The shape is: <tenantHost>/xWeb/secure/netFORUMXML.asmx (SOAP) or <tenantHost>/xWeb/JSON/<MethodName> (JSON shim). The BaseURL is stored in the per-CompanyIntegration credential (netforum-token.schema.json.BaseURL field). Source: credential schema + connector code ParseConfig() method + public WSDL endpoints (myasm.asm.org/xweb/secure/netforumxml.asmx, apconetforum.org/xweb/secure/netFORUMXML.asmx) confirming the path shape.
Configuration.routeNote: Disambiguates this connector from netFORUM Pro (different product with different API surface) and from the Higher Logic XML route. This connector targets netFORUM Enterprise via xWeb only. Source: SOURCE_STUDY.md Scope Decision + NetForumContext.md route taxonomy.

PaginationDefaults.description: xWeb GetQuery returns the full result set in a single call — there is no standard offset/limit/cursor pagination in the API protocol. The DataGrid row limit (see xWebDataGridRowLimitBehavior) is a server-side cap that TRUNCATES results silently when the result set exceeds the configured maximum. The connector must detect truncation (compare returned row count to the row limit) and split queries via date-range partitioning or other filters rather than assuming completeness. The PaginationType=None reflects the API protocol; the row-limit truncation is a separate concern documented in xWebDataGridRowLimitBehavior.
PaginationDefaults.xWebDataGridRowLimitBehavior: The xWeb DataGrid row limit is a configurable server-side ceiling on the number of rows returned by a single GetQuery call. Default is approximately 100-200 rows on older installations; some installations set it as high as 1000+. The exact limit is customer-configured in iWeb and is NOT discoverable via a credential-free API call. Behavior when the limit is hit: the response is silently truncated to the limit — the API does NOT return a pagination cursor, a "hasMore" flag, or any error. The connector MUST treat a response whose row count exactly equals a round-number boundary (e.g., exactly 100, 200, 500, 1000) as a potential truncation signal and implement date-range partitioning or object-specific szWhereClause filters to obtain the complete dataset. Source: SOURCE_STUDY.md Gaps section ("Row limit configuration ... customer-configured and not in the public WSDL. Only discoverable via sandbox testing."); Abila docs GetQuery page (documentation.abila.com) mentions "@TOP N" modifier for GetQuery object names (e.g., "Individual @TOP -1" for all rows, "Individual @TOP 5000" for a bounded count). The "@TOP -1" modifier in the szObjectName parameter bypasses the DataGrid row limit. EvidenceStrength: ImpliedFromExample.
PaginationDefaults.getTotalViaTopMinusOne: Use the szObjectName "@TOP -1" suffix (e.g., szObjectName="Individual @TOP -1") in GetQuery to bypass the DataGrid row limit and retrieve all records. Note: this may be slow on large datasets. Alternatively use "@TOP N" for incremental batching by date range. Source: Abila docs GetQuery.htm (documentation.abila.com/netforum-enterprise/2017.1/Content/xWeb/Methods/GetQuery.htm).

Configuration.IncrementalSyncDescription: NetForum xWeb supports incremental sync via the szWhereClause parameter on GetQuery. Each facade entity has its own prefixed last-modified timestamp column (e.g., ind_last_updated_dt for Individual, evt_last_updated_dt for Event). There is no universal watermark field name — the prefix varies per entity (ind_, evt_, reg_, cmt_, cmm_, etc.). The connector resolves the object-specific watermark column via the WSDL DataObjectType field names. Source: connector code (ResolveWatermarkColumn + ResolveDeclaredWatermarkColumn methods; NF_OBJECTS catalog listing ind_last_updated_dt, evt_start_dt per object). WSDL evidence: DateTime-typed fields ending in _dt present in Individual_*, EventsRegistrant_*, etc. DataObjectType schemas.
Configuration.IncrementalWatermarkFieldPatternNote: Each facade entity uses a prefixed last-updated column. Examples from the static catalog: ind_last_updated_dt (Individual), and per-type inference for others. The prefix matches the entity's column naming convention (ind_ = Individual, evt_ = EventsRegistrant, org_ = Organization, etc.). Source: connector NF_OBJECTS catalog + WSDL DataObjectType analysis. No single universal field name exists across all objects.
Configuration.WebhooksNote: NetForum Enterprise xWeb has no webhook or change-data-capture endpoint. The API is pull-based (GetQuery + incremental watermark). The connector comment in NetForumConnector.ts explicitly states: "Webhooks (NOT available) — no webhook/CDC support in NetForum". Source: connector code comment (Line 40: "Webhooks (NOT available)"); absence from WSDL (277 operations; none are subscription/push endpoints). EvidenceStrength: ImpliedFromExample (comprehensive absence from the WSDL is strong implied evidence).
Configuration.BulkOperationsNote: No batch/bulk mutation endpoint in xWeb. CRUD is per-record via InsertFacadeObject / UpdateFacadeObject. The WEBCentralizedShoppingCart* cluster (124 operations) handles multi-line-item order entry but these are transient cart operations, not bulk record mutation. Source: WSDL operation analysis (277 ops; no batch create/update endpoints). EvidenceStrength: ImpliedFromExample.
Configuration.APIVersioningStrategyNote: xWeb does not use URL-path versioning. The SOAP namespace http://www.avectra.com/2005/ encodes the Avectra-era year but is not versioned in the URL path. The WSDL endpoint is /xweb/secure/netforumxml.asmx?WSDL with no version segment. Backward compatibility is maintained across Community Brands releases by adding new operations without removing or changing existing ones. Source: WSDL URL patterns on public instances (myasm.asm.org, apconetforum.org). EvidenceStrength: ImpliedFromExample.
Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: There is no OAuth2-style refresh_token. When the session token expires, the connector re-authenticates from scratch by calling /xWeb/JSON/Authenticate again with the stored Basic credentials. The connector maintains a token cache with a 1-hour TTL (ExpiresAt = Date.now() + 3600*1000) and re-authenticates before the TTL elapses. A 401 response on any call triggers an immediate token invalidation and re-authentication retry. Source: connector code (tokenCache, Authenticate method lines 320-357; 401 handling in MakeHTTPRequest line 476: "if (response.status === 401 && attempt === 0) { this.tokenCache = null; continue; }").

ErrorResponseShape.description: NetForum xWeb JSON mode returns HTTP 4xx/5xx with error details in various forms depending on the endpoint and xWeb version. Common patterns: (1) SOAP fault wrapped in JSON; (2) {"ExceptionMessage": "...", "ExceptionType": "...", "Message": "..."} for .NET-style errors; (3) Plain HTTP status codes with no body for auth failures. SOAP mode returns standard SOAP Fault elements. The connector handles non-200 responses by inspecting status codes and surfacing the raw body. Source: connector code MakeHTTPRequest error handling; EvidenceStrength: ImpliedFromExample (inferred from .NET/SOAP stack patterns; exact shapes require sandbox verification).

WriteCapability.description: InsertFacadeObject and UpdateFacadeObject are documented in the WSDL (ExplicitStatement). DeleteFacadeObject appears in the WSDL as an operation name but is NOT confirmed in any reachable vendor documentation page. The connector sets SupportsDelete=false and routes DeleteRecord to a best-effort call that returns an error rather than silently claiming success. The vendor appears to prefer "soft delete" via status flags. Source: connector code comment lines 143-147 ("Vendor docs document InsertFacadeObject + UpdateFacadeObject; no DeleteFacadeObject appears in any reachable doc page ... Keeping the flag false until DeleteFacadeObject is confirmed"). WSDL evidence for Create/Update: InsertFacadeObject, UpdateFacadeObject operations present (ExplicitStatement).
WriteCapability.WritePathNote: All mutations route through the FacadeObject generic interface. Entity-specific WEB* operations (e.g., WEBIndividualInsert, WEBOrganizationInsert, WEBContactRequestInsert) exist in the WSDL for a subset of entities but the connector uses InsertFacadeObject as the universal Create path. The FacadeObject interface accepts szObjectName + oRecord parameters.

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: xWeb exposes no ETag, If-Match, version counter, or optimistic-lock header on GetFacadeObject or UpdateFacadeObject responses. The API is last-write-wins. Conflict handling relies on snapshot-3-way diff at the MJ sync layer, not on vendor-side locking. Source: WSDL operation analysis (no ETag/version fields in DataObjectType schemas); connector code (no If-Match header sent). EvidenceStrength: ImpliedFromExample.
Configuration.DeleteSemanticsNote: NetForum uses status flags rather than hard record deletion for most entities. The connector comment explicitly notes: "NetForum more commonly uses status flags (soft delete) rather than hard delete" (NetForumConnector.ts line 145-146). The specific status flag name varies by entity type (e.g., active/inactive flag in Individual, Membership status fields). Hard delete via DeleteFacadeObject is unconfirmed from documentation. Source: connector code comments; EvidenceStrength: ImpliedFromExample.
Configuration.DeleteStatusFlagNote: The soft-delete field name varies per entity type. Exact field names for each entity require sandbox verification. Common patterns in AMS systems include: active_flag, status_code, or equivalent. The WSDL DataObjectType schemas contain boolean/status fields but the specific "deleted" indicator is installation-dependent.
Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Read-only by default. Write capability (InsertFacadeObject / UpdateFacadeObject) is confirmed in the WSDL but bidirectional sync must be explicitly validated against a customer sandbox before enabling. No ETag/version concurrency control exists, making conflict resolution purely snapshot-based. Source: provable-only discipline; connector SupportsDelete=false.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionNote: No ETag or version field in xWeb responses precludes MostRecent-based conflict resolution. DestWins (the external system wins) is the safer default for an AMS system where the source of record is the vendor. If bidirectional is enabled, manual review may be preferred for membership-critical fields. Source: ConcurrencyControl=none (no version field → cannot reliably determine which change is most recent).

universalPK.pattern: Each NetForum facade entity has a GUID primary key named with the entity prefix and abbreviation (e.g., ind_cst_key for Individual, org_cst_key for Organization, mbr_key for Membership, evt_key for Event, reg_key for EventRegistration). The key is always a GUID string. The naming convention is <table_abbreviation>_key or <parent_abbreviation>_cst_key. Source: connector NF_OBJECTS catalog + WSDL DataObjectType schemas. Note: unlike REST APIs with a universal "id" field, netFORUM uses entity-specific key names.
universalPK.note: The runtime SoftPKClassifier should look for the <entity>_key or <entity>_cst_key pattern. The _cst_key suffix indicates a Customer Key (customer GUID) which is the FK shared across Individual and Organization.

RuntimeDiscoveryMechanism.CustomerQueries: GetQueryDefinition(szObjectName) returns the underlying SQL join structure (obj_key, obj_name, obj_description, ListTable, ListFromTables elements). Call with each customer-specific query name to discover its schema. Requires authentication.
RuntimeDiscoveryMechanism.CustomerViews: ExecuteMethod(szMethodName) can call customer-installed stored procedures and views. The method names are customer/partner-specific and must be discovered via customer documentation or admin questionnaire.
RuntimeDiscoveryMechanism.CustomColumns: GetFacadeXMLSchema(szObjectName) returns the XSD schema for a facade object including custom fields added by the customer. Requires authentication.
RuntimeDiscoveryMechanism.HigherLogicStoredProcs: HigherLogic-specific stored procedures (HigherLogic_GetChangedMembers, HigherLogic_GetMemberInfo, HigherLogic_GetChangedMeetings) are callable via ExecuteMethod only when the HL integration is installed. Presence is detected at connection time, not declared as static metadata.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies: HigherLogic partner stored procedures (HigherLogic_GetChangedMembers, HigherLogic_GetMemberInfo, HigherLogic_GetChangedMeetings) — partner-installed, runtime-Discovered only
Custom customer query objects via GetQuery — customer-installation-specific, runtime-Discovered
Customer-specific SQL views via ExecuteMethod — installation-specific
Custom WEB* methods from customer extension WSDL files (e.g. <acronym>_WS.asmx)
Configuration.ScopeReason: The 34 COVERABLE families are provable from the public WSDL (HTTP 200, credential-free, 5.9 MB, 277 ops, 434 DataObjectType schemas confirmed across two independent live instances). Customer-specific queries, Higher Logic partner stored procedures, and custom extension WSDL files are runtime-Discovered at connection time via GetQueryDefinition/ExecuteMethod introspection — not declared as static metadata because their presence, names, and schemas vary per customer installation. MemberDirectory ops (WEBMemberDirectorySearch, WEBMemberDirectoryOrganizationSearch) return Individual/Organization subsets and are classified under those entities rather than as a separate IO.
Configuration.CustomObjectMarkerPattern: null — xWeb does not expose a machine-readable custom-object marker. Custom objects and views installed via iWeb/DBA are discoverable only via GetQueryDefinition at runtime. No naming convention is enforced for custom objects.
Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerPattern: null — Custom fields in a facade object are returned alongside standard fields from GetFacadeObject/GetQuery. The XSD schema from GetFacadeXMLSchema reveals custom fields at runtime but there is no credential-free marker pattern. Custom fields may follow installation-specific naming conventions.
